Bright
brīt
adj. (shining, clear; rendering Hebrew bahir, Greek lampros)
Old English beorht. Brightness in Scripture attaches to swords, clouds, and finally to a title Christ gives Himself.

Biblical Definition

Bright means shining. Christ names Himself with it at the very end of Scripture: “I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star” (Rev 22:16). Hebrews says the Son is “the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person” (Heb 1:3). A bright cloud overshadows the mount of transfiguration (Mat 17:5), and Ezekiel sees a brightness about the throne like the appearance of the bow in the cloud (Eze 1:28).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines bright as shining; lucid; luminous; splendid; resplendent; and clear, transparent, as liquors; also, evident, clear, manifest to the mind.

expand to see more

BRIGHT, a. Shining; lucid; luminous; splendid; as a bright sun or star; a bright metal.

2. Clear; transparent; as liquors.

3. Evident; clear; manifest to the mind, as light is to the eyes.

4. Resplendent with charms.

Key Scripture

Rev 22:16 — "I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star."

Heb 1:3 — "Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;"

Mat 17:5 — "While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him."

Eze 1:28 — "As the appearance of the bow that is in the cloud in the day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness round about. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. And when I saw it, I fell upon my face, and I heard a voice of one that spake."

Modern Corruption

Christ is pictured chiefly in humility, and the last self-description in Scripture is the bright and morning star — the light that appears when the night is nearly over.

expand to see more

Revelation 22:16 is Christ's own final self-designation: I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star. The morning star rises last and is brightest, and it appears when the night is at its longest but nearly done. The title is chosen for a church waiting, and it is followed two verses later by the invitation to whosoever will.

Hebrews 1:3 uses the word for the relation between the Son and the Father: who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person. Brightness here is not reflected light but radiance proceeding from its source — the beam is of one substance with the sun and cannot be separated from it. The whole doctrine of the Son's deity is compressed into a metaphor about light.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew bahir (H925), bright; nogah (H5051), brightness; Greek lampros (G2986), bright; apaugasma (G541), effulgence, in Hebrews 1:3.

expand to see more

Greek lampros (G2986) — bright, radiant; Revelation 22:16, Acts 10:30.

Greek apaugasma (G541) — brightness, effulgence; only Hebrews 1:3.

Hebrew nogah (H5051) — brightness; Ezekiel 1:28, Isaiah 60:3.

Usage

"“The bright and morning star” — the last self-description in Scripture."

"“The brightness of his glory” — radiance of one substance with its source."

"“A bright cloud overshadowed them” — the transfiguration."
